per_policy_guidance.guidance:
**Primary/default candidate within the demonstrated entry distribution.** This dual-source/bowl-position, absolute-world-orientation policy satisfied the required final stage exit in 11/12 validation runs (91.7%). At the final state, all 12 runs were upright with zero particles in the bowl; 11/12 were also over the bowl. The sole failure remained upright and spill-free but did not reach the bowl footprint. All runs reported zero IK-unconverged steps.

Invoke only with finite, trustworthy container and bowl poses; nominally with an upright, table-supported source and open fingers, or from a nearby closed/low/lifted state when source/TCP co-motion is plausible. Handle geometry must be unchanged and the target must be reachable with collision clearance. The prior is designed to combine source-relative acquisition, bowl-relative staging, and absolute orientation, but robustness to displaced objects or other out-of-distribution states was not tested.

Avoid or stop for noisy/missing poses, changed geometry, large rotations, obstacles, unreachable configurations, grasp miss, slip/drop, or severe intermediate-state error. Recognize failure through closed fingers without source/TCP co-motion, failure to lift, abrupt or stalled transport, particle escape, loss of uprightness, staging outside the bowl footprint, IK nonconvergence, or joint-limit contact. Do not treat the internal destination/blend weight as proof of contact or phase.

Hand off to `controlled_pour_and_right` only when physical observations confirm closed fingers, source/TCP co-motion, table clearance, an upright container high over the bowl, and no particle in the bowl. If the container is upright but not over the bowl—as in the one validation failure—do not hand off; stop/escalate or reselect.

**Secondary candidate for phase-ambiguous nominal entries.** This bowl-frame policy with causal phase supervision met the full stage exit in 7/12 validation runs (58.3%). Every run ended upright with zero particles in the bowl, but 5/12 failed because the container was not over the bowl. All runs had zero IK-unconverged steps. Prefer its documented niche when entering near demonstrated approach, just after closure, or already lifted and the grasp/lift phase is ambiguous; use h04 instead when a broadly stronger validated exit rate is desired.

Require finite container/bowl poses and corroborate phase using finger width, source elevation, and source/TCP co-motion. Avoid for a strongly displaced ungrasped source, large source/bowl rotations, noisy or reordered phase observations, missed grasps, slips, changed geometry, obstacles, or unreachable targets. These cases are unsupported, and no out-of-distribution phase-recovery result exists.

Failure is most directly recognized when the source remains upright but does not reach the bowl footprint, matching all five validation failures. Also stop for phase inference inconsistent with finger/elevation/co-motion evidence, closed fingers without source motion, drop, early particle escape, IK nonconvergence, or limit contact. The auxiliary phase class is not contact evidence.

Hand off to `controlled_pour_and_right` only on observed closure, source/TCP co-motion, table clearance, upright high staging over the bowl, and no particle in the bowl; never hand off merely because the phase head indicates “lifted.”

**Low-priority, nominal-support-only option.** This source-frame policy is intended for source-table-pose displacement, but that intended out-of-distribution benefit was not validated. From the 12 demonstrated entry states it met the full final exit in only 2/12 runs (16.7%). It ended over the bowl in 9/12 and with zero particles in the bowl in 12/12, but only two runs combined over-bowl staging with uprightness; three runs failed to stage over the bowl, and those three included substantial IK nonconvergence (142–321 unconverged steps).

Use only cautiously when the source is upright and observable, the gripper is open or a prior close has plausible source/TCP co-motion, and measured joints admit the source-relative target. Do not prefer it merely because the source is displaced: displacement robustness is a design intent, not a measured result. Avoid large source rotations, changed handle geometry, obstacles, unreachable placements, grasp misses, slips, or any state outside the demonstrated support.

Recognize failure through persistent TCP/handle misalignment, fingers remaining open, closure without source/TCP co-motion, failure to clear the table or reach the bowl, loss of uprightness, independent particle motion, IK nonconvergence, or limit contact. Do not interpret closure alone as a grasp.

Nominal handoff to `controlled_pour_and_right` requires closed fingers, verified co-motion, table clearance, upright high staging over the bowl, and no particle in the bowl. The documented overlap permits an earlier successor transition after a clearly secure lift, but the conservative choice is the validated high-stage exit; never hand off on closure alone.

**Do not select for autonomous completion of this stage under the current evidence.** The fresh-TCP incremental policy passed 0/12 validation runs. It did place the container over the bowl with zero particles in the bowl in all 12 and had zero IK-unconverged steps, but the container was not upright in any run, so it never met the exit rule.

Its documented niche is a nearby demonstrated approach/grasp/lift/carry configuration or a local TCP correction, with two finite causal frames, an upright source, and either open fingers or plausible closed-finger co-motion. That niche is a design intent only: no deliberately perturbed or out-of-distribution recovery trial exists. Avoid for any invocation that needs a validated upright handoff, and avoid large source displacement, severe phase ambiguity, grasp misses, slips, changed geometry, obstacles, or unreachable targets. Incremental errors may accumulate.

Recognize the validated failure signature as reaching the bowl while losing uprightness. Also stop for repeated local motion without reducing handle error, open fingers during lift, source/TCP disagreement, early particle separation, IK nonconvergence, or limit contact.

Being over the bowl is insufficient for handoff. Transfer to `controlled_pour_and_right` only if independent physical observations nevertheless verify closed fingers, source/TCP co-motion, table clearance, upright high staging over the bowl, and no particle in the bowl. Because validation never reached that complete condition, there is no measured evidence of a successful handoff-producing run.

summary:
Validation covers only execution from each policy’s own training-segment entry states across 12 demonstrations, for the fixed budget and final-state exit rule; it contains no out-of-distribution evidence and does not establish recovery from misses, slips, obstacles, pose noise, geometry changes, or unreachable targets. These are stage-exit results, not full-task success results.

Recommended order within nominal demonstrated support: **h04 first (11/12)**, **h03 second (7/12)**, **h01 only cautiously (2/12)**, and **do not use h02 for autonomous stage completion (0/12)**. h04’s lone miss and all five h03 misses were failure to finish over the bowl despite uprightness. h01 showed frequent orientation/staging failures and IK nonconvergence in its three non-staging runs. h02 consistently reached the bowl but was never upright. No final validation state had a particle in the bowl.

For every policy, accept handoff to `controlled_pour_and_right` only from physical evidence: fingers closed around the source, source/TCP co-motion, table clearance, upright container high over the bowl, and zero particles in the bowl. Internal phase labels or blend weights and gripper closure alone are not contact evidence. On failed co-motion, slip/drop, premature particle motion, non-upright or off-bowl staging, IK nonconvergence, or limit contact, withhold handoff and stop/escalate or reselect rather than assuming recovery.
